charts.title: EBIT by Banner
charts.annotation: SegmentEBIT is only disclosed from FY2020; e&s (JB Hi-Fi Australia's newest banner) only from FY2025.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by banner
segmentRevenue.content:
JB Hi-Fi Limited reports four segments: JB Hi-Fi Australia (consumer electronics, the original and largest banner), JB Hi-Fi New Zealand, The Good Guys (acquired 2016, whitegoods/appliances) and e&s (a small, recently-acquired commercial electrical/security installer).

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: JB Hi-Fi Australia and The Good Guys are close in revenue scale but sell different categories into different households; e&s only shows up from FY2025 and is too small yet to move the group total.

What to watch:

  • Whether The Good Guys (appliances, more cyclical with housing) grows in step with JB Hi-Fi Australia (electronics)
  • NZ as the smallest, most currency- and market-size-constrained banner
  • e&s scaling from a low base -- a rounding error today, a real driver only if it keeps growing

segmentEbit.title: EBIT by banner
segmentEbit.content:
Segment EBIT is disclosed for JB Hi-Fi Australia, JB Hi-Fi New Zealand and The Good Guys from FY2020 onward, and for e&s from FY2025.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: JB Hi-Fi Australia supplies the large majority of group EBIT despite running thin margins on volume; The Good Guys and NZ are smaller absolute contributors. e&s ran a small EBIT loss in FY2026 (H1 profit, full-year loss) -- normal for a small, recently-integrated acquisition, but worth tracking for whether it breaks even.

What to watch:

  • Whether NZ (historically the weakest banner, EBIT-negative as recently as FY2020) keeps its FY2021-onward profitability
  • e&s trending to a full-year profit
  • Any banner's EBIT growing materially faster or slower than its own revenue (margin mix shift)

segmentEbitMargin.title: EBIT margin by banner
segmentEbitMargin.content:
Each banner's segment EBIT divided by its own segment revenue -- the like-for-like profitability comparison the blended group margin hides.

For JB Hi-Fi Limited: JB Hi-Fi Australia and The Good Guys typically run mid-single-digit EBIT margins on high inventory turns; e&s's margin is volatile because it is small and its EBIT swings between a small profit and a small loss period to period.

What to watch:

  • Margin compression in JB Hi-Fi Australia, the group's largest profit source
  • Whether The Good Guys' margin holds up through appliance-cycle downturns
  • e&s's margin as it scales -- too few periods yet for a trend
